issues: Target validation/framework references are still too easy to read as externally validated/endorsed targets rather than internal target-record fields.

IFRS S2 GHG cross-industry metric category is boundary-disclosed (good), but the draft does not explicitly state that Scope 1/2/3 measurement approach (e.g., GHG Protocol) is not disclosed—this is implied via ‘records unavailable’ but could be made clearer to avoid perceived omission.

Financed emissions are disclosed as a single loans figure; the draft appropriately discloses the lack of perimeter detail, but the opening ‘covers portfolio emissions’ wording slightly overstates completeness.
unsupported_claims: “The disclosures are prepared with reference to IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 …” (general compliance-style framing without specifying what is and is not covered; acceptable only if clearly positioned as ‘prepared with reference’ and not as full compliance).
Target ‘Third-party validation’ statements risk being read as assurance/validation of the Bank’s targets rather than a target-record field, even though later limitations attempt to narrow this.
material_unsupported_claims: “Third-party validation: … SBTi identified as the validation body” / “UNEP FI identified as the validation body” presented as if the targets are validated by those bodies. The only supported fact is that the target record flags third_party_validated=true and names a validation body; this must be framed more explicitly as ‘recorded in the target record’ and not as an external validation conclusion.

“Framework: … SBTi 1.5°C pathway” and “NZBA … framework” could be interpreted as confirmed alignment/acceptance by those initiatives. Without methodology/acceptance evidence, this must be framed strictly as the framework field in the target record (not as confirmed alignment or membership-based validation).
minor_wording_to_tighten: “It covers portfolio emissions …” could be tightened to avoid implying full portfolio coverage, because the financed-emissions perimeter is explicitly not disclosed.

“These metrics are used internally to … inform risk management, client engagement and strategic planning.” (fine, but could be tightened to avoid implying systematic integration across all processes without further support).
“Climate-related capital expenditure … directed towards climate-related initiatives …” and similar for opex: acceptable, but could be tightened given the absence of classification methodology detail.
correctly_disclosed_evidence_boundaries: Operational Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions for 2024 are not disclosed because detailed records are unavailable.
Financed-emissions perimeter (asset class/sector coverage and exclusions) is not separately disclosed.
No sector/geography/asset-class disaggregation of financed emissions is provided.
Detailed calculation methodologies, data quality assessments and key assumptions for metrics are not described.
Financed emissions, exposure metrics and climate-related financial metrics have not been independently verified.
Progress indicators are internal target-record metrics and have not been independently verified.
